My thoughts? This is their next "diversity" push, for all games to be inclusive of people of all skill levels, otherwise they are somehow displaying intolerance for lower-skilled players. I'm dead serious; that's how they're looking at it. Why would there be a fervor for multiple threads on the topic unless otherwise? I hate to tell this to the gaffots, but that's one diversity fight they're never going to win. Since the dawn of gaming there have ALWAYS been games that, by their very design, lock out players of certain insufficient skill level from either enjoying them at all, or enjoying them in a way fully intended by the designers, and there will ALWAYS be games that continue to do this in the future.

As in, EVERY game that's ever made, period. And guess what? That's a GOOD thing! If games accommodated all skill levels, they'd be the most watered-down pieces of tripe around. They would not have any particular soul to them, and just come off as if made on an assembly line by a focus group committee. That's already a problem so many Western AAA games suffer as-is, particularly many of the WRPG and open world-style games....sure as hell wouldn't want that spilling over into fighters.

Speaking of which, the very foundation of fighting games depends on utilizing all of the various game mechanics to outplay and defeat your opponent. By their very nature, they can't be "casual-inclusive" to the degree gaffots are crying for them to. Yeah, throw a Story mode in there, maybe some knockoff bowling games and shit, etc. But when I see them championing shit like what Capcom's seemingly doing w/ MvC:I (and it's oversimplification of button schemes), praising things like "no charge characters" etc., I just want to stab my eyes out. These idiots don't realize that it's NOT the button input complexity that keeps them among the bottom tier of players in these games; it's their lack of understanding on fundamentals, reads, spacing/zoning, defense/offense, whiff punish, buffering, anti-air, "feeling" their opponent etc. None of those things are intrinsically linked to the control scheme, so you're still going to end up with situations of the better players steamrolling gaffots. In fact, it'll be even WORST now, b/c the better players have less "barriers" (I don't see them that way myself; there's a methodology behind 360 and charge-based characters most people don't understand) to inhibit them, and that means they'll learn the meta game (and implement it) that much faster, giving gaffots and other casuals less time to even appreciate their mediocrity.

Well, that's just something I wanted to get off my chest, b/c it's clear GAF has a new agenda of some new "gaming injustice" to fight, but this is the most unrealistic fight they've engaged in to date, and will be the one they most clearly lose.
